ruleset.name: jpinpoint-remoting-rules
ruleset.description: jPinpoint rule set for performance aware Kotlin coding, sponsored by Rabobank.

rule.name: AvoidInMemoryStreamingDefaultConstructor
rule.message: The default capacity or smaller is used for ByteArrayOutputStream or StringWriter, it usually needs expensive expansions.
rule.description: The default constructor of ByteArrayOutputStream creates a 32-byte initial capacity and for StringWriter 16 chars. Problem: Such a small buffer as capacity usually needs several expensive expansions. Solution: Pre-size the ByteArrayOutputStream or StringWriter with an initial capacity such that an expansion is not needed in most cases, typically much larger than 32, for instance, 4096. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidStringBuffer
rule.message: StringBuffer is used. It introduces locking overhead, use StringBuilder.
rule.description: Problem: StringBuffer introduces locking overhead because it is thread safe. Its thread-safety is rarely needed. Solution: Replace StringBuffer by StringBuilder. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidDecimalAndChoiceFormatAsField
rule.message: Avoid using NumberFormat, DecimalFormat or ChoiceFormat as field since it is thread-unsafe.
rule.description: Problem: java.text.DecimalFormat and java.text.ChoiceFormat are thread-unsafe. Solution: usual solution is to create a new local one when needed in a method. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidRecompilingPatterns
rule.message: Pattern.compile is used in a method. Compiling a regex pattern can be expensive, make it a constant or instance field.
rule.description: A regular expression is compiled on every invocation. Problem: this can be expensive, depending on the length of the regular expression. Solution: Usually a pattern is a literal, not dynamic and can be compiled only once. Assign it to a private constant or instance field. java.util.Pattern objects are thread-safe so they can be shared among threads. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: MDCPutWithoutRemove
rule.message: MDC put is used without remove or clear in the same function
rule.description: MDC values are added for logging, but no corresponding remove or clear is performed. Problem: MDC values can leak to other user transactions (requests) and log incorrect information. Solution: remove the MDC value in a finally clause or clear the MDC. (jpinpoint-rules - Kotlin)

property.name: xpath

rule.name: AvoidRecompilingXPathExpression
rule.message: XPathExpression is created and compiled every time. Beware it is thread-unsafe.
rule.description: XPathExpression is created and compiled on every method call, compiled possibly implicitly by XPath::evaluate. Problem: Creation of XPath and compilation of XPathExpression takes time. It may slow down your application. Solution: 1. Avoid XPath usage. 2. Compile the xpath expression as String into a XPathExpression. However, since XPath and XPathExpression classes are thread-unsafe, they are not easily cached. Caching it in a ThreadLocal may be a solution. (jpinpoint-rules)

property.name: xpath

rule.name: AvoidSimpleDateFormat
rule.message: SimpleDateFormat is used. Since it is thread-unsafe, it needs expensive recreation.
rule.description: Problem: java.util.SimpleDateFormat is thread-unsafe. The usual solution is to create a new one when needed in a method. Creating SimpleDateFormat is relatively expensive. Solution: Use java.time.DateTimeFormatter. These classes are immutable, thus thread-safe and can be made static. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidMultipleConcatStatements
rule.message: Multiple statements concatenate to the same String. Use StringBuilder append.
rule.description: Multiple statements concatenate to the same String. Problem: Each statement with one or more +-operators creates a hidden temporary StringBuilder, a char[] and a new String object, which all have to be garbage collected. Solution: Use StringBuilder.append. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidWideScopeXPathExpression
rule.message: XPathExpression targets a wide scope, this is potentially slow.
rule.description: The XPathExpression targets a wide scope since it starts with `//`. Problem: XPath has to search in a wide scope for occurrences, this may take a while. Solution: 1. Avoid XPath usage. 2. Make the scope as narrow as possible, do not start with `//`. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidRecreatingDateTimeFormatter
rule.message: Avoid recreating DateTimeFormatter, it is relatively expensive.
rule.description: Problem: Recreating a DateTimeFormatter is relatively expensive. Solution: org.joda.time.format.DateTimeFormatter or Java 8 java.time.DateTimeFormatter is thread-safe and can be shared among threads. Create the formatter from a pattern only once, to initialize a constant or instance field. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidLoadingAllFromFile
rule.message: Files.readAll methods and similar APIs load all bytes into memory: a risk of memory problems.
rule.description: Problem: APIs like Files.readAllBytes, Files.readAllLines, Files.readString, InputStream.readAllBytes, IOUtils.toByteArray, ByteArrayOutputStream.toByteArray load entire content into heap memory. This risks OutOfMemoryError, long GC pauses, and slow responses when processing large files. Solution: Use streaming APIs end-to-end, do not buffer whole files in memory. Note: Not a problem for small files. Use @SuppressWarnings("PMD.AvoidLoadingAllFromFile") then. (jpinpoint-rules)

import java.nio.file.Files import java.nio.file.Path
fun bad(path: Path): ByteArray = Files.readAllBytes(path) // bad fun good(path: Path) = Files.newInputStream(path).use { it.copyTo(System.out) } // good

rule.name: UnresolvedType
rule.message: A type cannot be resolved. Make sure all dependencies are available on the classpath.
rule.description: Problem: When analyzing Kotlin code, a type reference could not be resolved. This typically means a dependency is missing from the analysis classpath. Several rules (using typeIs, matchesSig) depend on type information; without it they may produce false positives or miss violations. Solution: Make sure all dependencies are available on the auxiliary classpath (--aux-classpath). Compile all source code before running PMD. Note: this rule requires kotlin-type-mapper for type resolution.

rule.name: BufferFileStreaming
rule.message: FileInputStream or FileOutputStream used without buffering. Wrap with BufferedInputStream or BufferedOutputStream.
rule.description: Problem: With FileInputStream and FileOutputStream, file access is not buffered. The stream is read-from/written-to file byte by byte, where each operating system call has its overhead, which makes it slow. Solution: Use buffering to read/write a chunk of bytes at once with much lower overhead. Use BufferedOutput/InputStream which has a buffer size of 8 kB by default to write at once. Make sure to close it after use. (jpinpoint-rules)

property.name: xpath

rule.example:
import java.io.BufferedInputStream import java.io.FileInputStream
fun bad(name: String): ByteArray = FileInputStream(name).use { it.readBytes() } // bad
fun good(name: String): ByteArray = BufferedInputStream(FileInputStream(name)).use { it.readBytes() } // ok

rule.name: BufferFilesNewStream
rule.message: Files.newInputStream or newOutputStream is not buffered.
rule.description: Problem: Files.newInputStream or Files.newOutputStream is not buffered. The stream is read from/written to file byte by byte, where each OS call has overhead making it slow. Solution: Wrap with BufferedInputStream / BufferedOutputStream, or use Files.newBufferedReader/newBufferedWriter. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: InitializeComparatorOnlyOnce
rule.message: A Comparator is initialized inside a method or lambda; initialize it once as a shared field.
rule.description: Problem: Creating Comparator instances repeatedly in functions is inefficient. Solution: Initialize the Comparator once as a companion object val or top-level val and reuse. For idiomatic Kotlin, prefer compareBy/compareByDescending at top-level or companion object. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidCalendarDateCreation
rule.message: A Calendar is used to get a Date or millis; this is expensive. Use LocalDate.now(), Instant.now() or System.currentTimeMillis().
rule.description: Problem: Calendar.getInstance() is expensive as it scans locale and timezone configuration. Using it just to get the current time or a Date object wastes CPU. Solution: Use java.time.LocalDate.now(), java.time.Instant.now() or System.currentTimeMillis() for timestamps. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidRecreatingSecurityProviders
rule.message: Avoid re-creating security providers in methods; register them once (e.g. in a companion object init block).
rule.description: Problem: Creating security providers (e.g. BouncyCastleProvider) is expensive and should be done once. Re-creating them in methods or lambdas wastes CPU and may cause duplicate registration warnings. Solution: Register the provider once in a companion object init block or a top-level property. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: EqualsOperationInconsistentWithHashCode
rule.message: equals applies case normalization that hashCode does not.
rule.description: Problem: normalizing text in equals but not in hashCode makes object identity inconsistent for hash-based collections. Solution: use the same normalization in both equals and hashCode. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: FieldOfHashCodeMissingInEquals
rule.message: A property is used in hashCode but not in equals.
rule.description: Problem: using a property in hashCode but omitting it from equals can make objects behave unexpectedly in hash-based collections. Solution: use the same relevant properties in both equals and hashCode. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: MissingFieldInEquals
rule.message: Property assigned from construction is missing in equals method.
rule.description: Problem: if a property that participates in object state is omitted from equals, object equality can become inconsistent. Solution: include all relevant constructed properties in equals and hashCode. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: MissingFieldInHashCode
rule.message: Equals uses a property which is missing in hashCode.
rule.description: Problem: using fewer properties in hashCode than in equals can degrade hash-based collection performance and violate expectations. Solution: use the same relevant properties in equals and hashCode. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: HashCodeOnlyCallsSuper
rule.message: hashCode only calls super.
rule.description: Problem: when equals is implemented, hashCode needs a consistent implementation too. If hashCode only calls super.hashCode(), equal objects may behave incorrectly in hash-based collections. Solution: implement hashCode using the same relevant properties as equals. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidInfiniteRecursion
rule.message: Avoid recursive calls without a proper stop condition.
rule.description: Problem: recursive calls without a clear stop condition can overflow the stack or loop forever. Solution: add a terminating condition or rewrite as iteration. (jpinpoint-rules)
